question: When was the restructuring of public distribution system as a targeted public distribution system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The restructuring of the public distribution system as the **targeted public distribution system** (TPDS) was implemented in **1997**.
 
• The TPDS aims to provide food grains to the poor at subsidized rates, ensuring food security for the most vulnerable sections of society.
 
• Under TPDS, households are classified into **Below Poverty Line** (BPL) and **Above Poverty Line** (APL) categories, with BPL families receiving higher subsidies.
 
• This system was introduced to enhance the efficiency of the public distribution system by targeting the benefits more accurately to those in need.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The public distribution system in India has been in existence since the Second World War and was expanded in the 1960s and 1970s as a universal scheme.
 
• The TPDS was **introduced as part of the economic reforms of the 1990s** to address inefficiencies and leakages in the universal public distribution system.
 
• State governments are responsible for identifying eligible families and distributing food grains through a network of fair price shops.
 
• Over the years, various measures, including the use of technology, have been implemented to improve transparency and reduce corruption in the TPDS.
